headline: India has tested its first open-air quantum-encrypted link, sending encryption keys 5.56 km through the air between two institutes in Gujarat.
score_reason: Official, verifiable national first, but a short-range trial with no outside review and limited reach beyond India.
importance_line: India now has a working open-air quantum key link to build toward satellite-secured communications, which matters first to Indian government and defence users and then to QNu Labs and BISAG-N, though 5.56 km is a modest distance and the figures are the ministry's own.
summary: ANI reports that India's electronics ministry announced on 3 Oct 2026 the country's first free-space quantum key distribution link, a method of sending encryption keys as light through open air so that any eavesdropping is detectable, run over 5.56 km between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar by the Bengaluru company QNu Labs on the night of 27-28 Sep 2026. The ministry says the link kept errors below 5 percent and produced keys at 230 to 260 bits per second, which were then used by a post-quantum encryption platform to scramble test messages, a step it describes as groundwork for longer and satellite-based quantum-secure networks.
notes: Trial 27-28 Sep 2026, but the news event is the ministry's release of 3 Oct 2026, so kept NEW. ANI relays an official release; figures are unreviewed.
